scope: All remaining native public members in manual-bindings.json, each assigned one primary reason. Source inspection, not a runtime parity claim. Explicit adapter mappings, support bindings, properties and JavaScript-only helpers are outside this inventory.

status_definitions.implemented: Browser implementation found in native registration or JS wrapper; not a blanket behavior/parity guarantee.
status_definitions.inherited: Browser resolves an inherited method rather than an own registration.
status_definitions.missing: No browser registration or JS implementation found in reviewed sources.
status_definitions.placeholder: Public JS method exists but returns a fixed placeholder.

groups.title: Defaults and validation still written in JavaScript
groups.reason: Wrappers implement defaults, integer ranges, enum domains, finite-value and arity checks. Simple defaults are already supported; compound/domain validation must be preserved or derived from source before removing the wrappers.
groups.next_step: Use existing IDL default handling; generalize source-derived validation for finite coordinates, enum/range checks and dependent defaults. Keep engine preconditions distinct from argument validation.

members.name: PhysicsBody.step
members.note: Native adapter rejects attached bodies before calling step; preserve this binding-specific precondition.

groups.title: Overloads, argument reshaping and call dispatch
groups.reason: The public call is not a single unambiguous member pointer: overload selection, argument reordering, convenience composition, or static-to-instance exposure is handwritten.
groups.next_step: Derive overload selection from shared native call bodies and model reusable argument/default transformations; preserve API semantics.

groups.title: Callback interfaces and lifetimes
groups.reason: Native interface bridges or std::function adapters retain JS callbacks, control lifetime, translate arguments/results and preserve identity. Evaluator conversion alone does not implement these different callback contracts.
groups.next_step: Define reusable callback/interface contracts once per shape, including ownership, error handling, cancellation and synchronous return validation.

groups.next_step: Derive factory dispatch and string conversion policies; retain small engine-specific load/lookup functions where they perform actual resource work.

groups.title: Binary spans and 64-bit number representation
groups.reason: A byte span needs pointer/length/ownership rules; 64-bit native values need an explicit JavaScript number conversion policy.
groups.next_step: Reuse byte-array/MemBlock policies with safe length and copy semantics; define signed/unsigned 64-bit numeric conversion consistently rather than using incidental casts.
